title: How to merge PDFs without uploading
description: Combine several PDF files into one in your browser, set the page order, and download the result, with no upload of your documents to a server.
lede: Join cover letters, scans and reports into one PDF, and keep the files on your own device.
problem: Many online mergers send your files to a server first, which is a poor fit for ID scans, contracts or anything private. A browser-based merger does the work on your own device, so the documents never need to leave it.

steps.title: Put the PDFs in one folder
steps.body: Give them names that sort in the order you want, such as 1-cover.pdf and 2-report.pdf. It saves reordering later.

steps.title: Open the PDF merger and add your files
steps.body: Choose one or more PDFs. You can add more in a second pick. Each file is checked on the way in; a damaged or non-PDF file shows an error and is not added.

steps.title: Set the order
steps.body: Use Up and Down to move a file, or Remove to drop it. The list from top to bottom is the page order of the merged document.

steps.title: Merge and download
steps.body: Select Merge and download. The tool copies every page, in list order, into one new PDF and saves it as merged.pdf.

steps.title: Open the result and check it
steps.body: Scroll through merged.pdf before you send it. Check page order, page count and that scans are readable. If something is wrong, use Clear and start again.

steps.title: Check for yourself that nothing is uploaded
steps.body: Open your browser's developer tools, go to the Network tab, then run a merge. You should see no request that sends your PDF out. This is a check you can repeat any time.

example: Add cover.pdf (1 page) and then report.pdf (3 pages). Merged in that order you get one 4-page PDF: the cover first, then the three report pages.
limitations: Limits are 25 MB per PDF, 20 files, and 80 MB combined. They protect your browser tab and are not a promise that every file under the limit will work.
Password-protected or encrypted PDFs are not supported. Unlock them first.
Forms, bookmarks and some advanced PDF features may not be kept exactly in the merged file.
Phones and tablets with little free memory can freeze or fail on large or image-heavy scans. Try a computer or merge in smaller batches.

faq.q: Are my PDFs sent to a server?
faq.a: No. The merge runs in your browser tab using the pdf-lib library. You can confirm it with the Network tab as described above.

faq.q: Can I change the order after adding the files?
faq.a: Yes. Use Up and Down on each file before you merge. The order shown is the order in the result.

faq.q: How do I split a PDF afterwards?
faq.a: Use the PDF splitter to extract page ranges into a new file.
